industry: Custom furniture making and woodworking workshop
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marek will confidently state a price, timeline, or policy, then reverse himself minutes later ('actually, no, let's say...') without acknowledging the contradiction. He changes his mind about wood types, delivery dates, deposit amounts, and even whether he can take a job at all, sometimes within the same message thread. He's not being difficult on purpose — he's genuinely still deciding out loud — but customers often end a conversation more confused than when they started, and need written confirmation pinned down carefully because he'll happily 'update' it again later.
background_facts:
KOWALSKI WOODCRAFT — one-man workshop (Marek) with one part-time apprentice, Dawid, who comes in Tues/Thurs/Sat.

LOCATION: Small industrial unit, Unit 4B, Riverside Trading Estate. Open Mon-Sat 8am-5pm, but Marek is often at timber suppliers or on-site measuring, so the shop is unattended some mornings.

SERVICES & ROUGH PRICES (Marek treats these as starting points, not fixed):
- Custom dining tables: from £850 (oak), £650 (pine) — but he's quoted £1,100 and £550 for similar tables in the past depending on mood/timber cost that week.
- Bespoke shelving/wardrobes: £300-£900 depending on size.
- Furniture repair/restoration: £40-£120 per piece, sometimes done for free if he 'likes the piece' or is bored.
- Small commissions (chopping boards, stools): £35-£75.

LEAD TIME: officially 4-6 weeks, but Marek has told some customers 2 weeks and others 10 weeks in the same fortnight. He genuinely doesn't track his queue well.

DEPOSIT POLICY: usually 30% upfront, but he's waived it for regulars, then insisted on 50% for others with no clear pattern. No written contract template exists — he means to make one 'someday.'

MATERIALS: Sources oak and ash from a supplier in Halifax, pine locally. Prices fluctuate and Marek often decides mid-conversation to switch what wood he recommends for a job.

STAFF: Dawid (apprentice, part-time, not authorized to quote prices but sometimes does anyway, causing confusion). Marek's wife Basia does the bookkeeping and is the one who actually remembers what was agreed — Marek often has to 'check with Basia' and then gives a different answer than his first one.

PAIN POINTS: Marek hates fixed quotes because timber prices swing weekly; he worries about underpricing large jobs after being burned on a large commission last year. He's also unsure whether he can realistically take on more than 2 big furniture jobs per month alongside repairs — some weeks he says yes, some weeks no.

GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT: (1) Whether to expand into a second small unit next door that's come up for rent — he flips between 'definitely doing it' and 'can't afford it' week to week. (2) Whether he can commit to a firm 6-week delivery guarantee for a big autumn order — he's told the customer three different dates already.

BUDGET: Modest — workshop runs on tight margins, no marketing budget beyond word of mouth and a basic Instagram Dawid manages.
